project.khorgos-gateway-dry-port.summary: Kazakh railway dry port on the Chinese border where containers switch between Chinese and Russian-gauge trains; COSCO Shipping and Lianyungang Port bought 49% of it in 2017.
project.kuryk-port.summary: Kazakh state-built Caspian rail-ferry terminal and rail spur south of Aktau, serving the Trans-Caspian route to Baku without Chinese finance.
project.angren-pap-railway.summary: Electrified line through the 19 km Qamchiq tunnel, dug by China Railway Tunnel Group with a China Exim Bank loan, linking the Fergana Valley to Tashkent without crossing Tajikistan.
project.kti-railway.summary: 925 km line from Uzen through western Turkmenistan to Gorgan, built by the three governments without Chinese finance, giving Central Asia a direct rail route to the Gulf.
project.baku-tbilisi-kars-railway.summar: Rail link across the Caucasus with a gauge-change station at Akhalkalaki, financed mainly by Azerbaijani loans to Georgia and by Türkiye, and opened in October 2017.
project.baku-alat-port: Baku International Sea Trade Port at Alat
project.baku-alat-port.summary: Azerbaijan's state-funded new Caspian port and free trade zone south of Baku, replacing the old city-centre port.
project.gwadar-port.summary: Deep-water port in Balochistan run by China Overseas Port Holding Company since 2013, with a CPEC free zone and expressway, where traffic has stayed low amid local protests and insurgent attacks.
project.kkh-havelian-thakot.summary: 118 km upgrade of Pakistan's road to the Chinese border, built by China Road and Bridge Corporation with a concessional Chinese loan.
project.sahiwal-coal.summary: 1,320 MW imported-coal plant in Punjab built by China Huaneng and Shandong Ruyi under CPEC, easing power cuts at the cost of high emissions.
project.port-qasim-coal.summary: 1,320 MW coal plant near Karachi owned by PowerChina and Qatar's Al Mirqab Capital and financed by China Exim Bank.
project.lahore-orange-line.summary: Pakistan's first metro line, 27 km long, built by a China Railway–Norinco consortium with a China Exim Bank loan after court disputes over demolitions near heritage sites.
project.piraeus-cosco.summary: COSCO Shipping bought 51% of the Piraeus Port Authority in 2016 during Greece's debt-crisis privatisations and raised its stake to 67% in 2021.
project.great-stone-park.summary: Special economic zone near Minsk developed with China Merchants Group and Chinese loans, offering tax breaks to manufacturing, tech and logistics firms.
project.yamal-lng.summary: Arctic LNG plant led by Novatek with CNPC (20%) and the Silk Road Fund (9.9%) as partners, financed by Chinese banks after Western sanctions in 2014.
project.power-of-siberia.summary: Gazprom pipeline carrying Siberian gas to China under a 30-year contract signed with CNPC in 2014; Russian-financed and negotiated since the 2000s, it is treated as a bilateral energy deal rather than a Belt and Road project.
project.ankara-istanbul-hsr.summary: Eskişehir–Istanbul section built by a CRCC-led consortium with a China Exim Bank loan; contracted in the mid-2000s, it predates the Belt and Road.
project.kumport-terminal.summary: COSCO Pacific, China Merchants and CIC bought 65% of Kumport, Istanbul's third-largest container terminal, in 2015.
project.nac-cbd.summary: Twenty towers, including Africa's tallest building, built by China State Construction Engineering Corporation east of Cairo with Chinese bank loans.
project.teda-suez-zone.summary: Chinese-developed industrial park at Ain Sokhna in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, whose 6 km² expansion area was launched in January 2016.
project.tehran-mashhad-electrification.s: Plan to electrify Iran's busiest 926 km main line with Chinese contractors and a China Exim Bank loan, stalled after US sanctions returned in 2018.
project.marmaray.summary: Japanese-financed rail tunnel under the Bosporus linking Türkiye's Asian and European networks, opened in October 2013; the first China–Europe freight train used it in 2019.
